head.title: The scanner never gets a vote on whether it was right
head.lede: There are ten test methods, and one rule holds for all of them.

theRule.title: Write down the answer first. Then run it.
lede: Every method insists the expected result is authored, reviewed and hashed

lede.b: Without that order, the numbers mean nothing

rows.body: “A scanner result must never create or revise ground truth.”
“…rather than inferring validity from scanner agreement.”
“Recalculate spans from construction, never by searching scanner output.”
“Never relabel a control because a competitor flags it.”
“Majority agreement cannot promote, demote, or rewrite an expectation.”

p: Scanners never see the answer: adapters get only the fixture's identity and its bytes,

p.b: never the expectation, never the evidence tier.

howAResultIsGraded.title: Five answers, not two
lede: “Did it find the secret?” is too blunt. The true span is known to the byte, so the grade asks

rows.description: Redacts the whole secret plus one byte either side, within the allowance
Redacts the secret but takes surrounding text beyond the allowance
Redacts part of the secret; the last byte leaks

claimSub: : swallowing the paragraph around the key hides the key but ruins the log line. Only a span inside its authored allowance passes.
howAResultIsGraded.claim: Catching 31 of 32 bytes is a leak, not a near miss.

theTenMethods.title: Each one looks for a different way to be wrong
lede: They are numbered because they run in order: everything after the first is
from it. You cannot write a twin without a canonical positive to twin.

phases.title: Then check it only takes what it should
phases.body: a detector that matches more text looks better on positives alone

phases.title: Then attack it
phases.body: edges, characters, containers, and machine-made variants

phases.title: Then look outward, and forward
phases.body: other tools, unseen cases, and the passage of time

methods.title: Canonical positive
methods.ask: Does it find the easy one?
gist: The seed every other method grows from. Byte ranges, evidence and source hash are recorded
a scanner runs.

gist.b: Passing this alone earns no support claim.

methods.title: Negative twin
methods.ask: Change exactly one thing. Does it go quiet?
gist: One mutation only: prefix, length, alphabet, boundary or public-prefix. Two changes is not a twin. The pair is scored as
, so you cannot win by flagging everything.

methods.title: Boundary cases
methods.ask: What happens one character either side of the rule?
gist: Every documented length and delimiter needs a case

it, or a written reason why that pair is meaningless. This catches off-by-one ranges and accidental substring matches, down to end of file, a missing final newline, CRLF, and a key touching the next token.

methods.title: Alphabet mutations
methods.ask: Is it really checking the body, or just the prefix and the length?
gist: One character swapped, everything else held still. A cheap detector that only checks “right prefix, roughly right length” fails

methods.title: Context permutations
methods.ask: Same key, different wrapper. Same answer?
gist: bare · .env · JSON · YAML · TOML · source code · Markdown · URI · quoted · CRLF. The credential bytes do not change; everything around them does. The expected answer must
. Each context is reported separately, so strong results in one cannot hide a weak one.

methods.title: Benign lookalikes
methods.ask: Does it stay silent on things that merely look like keys?
gist: Each is deliberately close to the real thing and probes one specific way to overmatch. Policy-based controls are counted in a
from source-backed ones, so a judgement call cannot dilute a fact.

methods.ask: What about the thousand variants nobody would hand-write?
gist: The spec says this is

methods.title: Holdout evaluation
methods.ask: How does it do on cases it was never tuned against?
gist: This is the exam nobody studied for. The ordinary development command
the holdout corpus. The candidate is frozen before the cases are revealed, and touching it afterwards voids the run. A newer rule closes the last loophole:

gist.b: holdout results may never be used to pick scorer thresholds or weights

methods.title: Regression freeze
methods.ask: Could we quietly break this next month?
gist: A finished run becomes an immutable comparison point (
: fixture hashes, versions, every outcome). A new
or false alarm fails the build. An intentional change needs
before the baseline moves, and improvements never erase the old record.

theEscapeHatch.title: There is a third answer
lede: Real formats are ambiguous at the edges. A suite that forces every case into pass or fail
So these methods keep a third answer.

cards.body: Still a secret after the change. Must be caught.
No longer a secret. Must be ignored.

p: A review-required case makes no pass or fail claim and never enters an average. The same goes for
evidence, which can be observed and inspected but is deliberately left unscored.
note: otherwise ambiguity gets settled by looking at what the scanners did, and the whole suite exists to break that loop.

whatItAllBuys.title: Even with all ten green

cards.body: That on these exact bytes, at this exact version, with these pinned tool versions, the scanner behaved as reviewers said it should, and anyone can reproduce that from a clean checkout.

body: Production accuracy. Method 01 says so outright: this is
coverage. Method 09 adds that holdout does not establish production accuracy either.

body.b: Ten green methods describe the corpus, not real-world traffic.

p: No single method is enough on its own. That is also why the support matrix grades a family on
